apparatus.basis: ⲕⲣⲓ restored by editor; ⲧⲏⲥ visible. ⲕⲣⲓⲧⲏⲥ (Greek κριτής 'judge') is the central term debated throughout the chapter — the Apostle has just asserted that God is a judge, prompting the Nazorean's challenge.
ⲧ restored, ⲏⲥ visible; the word ⲕⲣⲓⲧⲏⲥ continues from line 3 ⲉⲧⲉⲣⲉ ⲕⲣⲓ-
ⲛ̄ restored, ϩⲏⲧⲟⲩ visible; locative 'in/among them' completing the previous line's reference to the men beaten with the whip
initial ⲉ restored, ⲥⲧⲉ visible; Greek loanword ὥστε in Lycopolitan form ⲉⲥⲧⲉ 'so that, therefore'
ⲉ visible, ⲛ restored; the Coptic negation ⲉⲛ closing the predicate 'a doer-of-wickedness is not the judge'
final ⲉ of ⲙⲛⲧⲃⲟⲟⲛⲉ; word completion only
ⲟⲩⲧ restored, ⲙⲟⲩ visible; standard Coptic ⲙⲟⲩⲟⲩⲧ 'kill' fits the verb-series ϩⲱⲧⲃⲉ ('slay') ⲙⲟⲩⲟⲩⲧ ('kill')
ⲱ restored medially; ⲡⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'the man' from whom the evil is severed
ⲟⲩ restored, ⲧⲉ visible; Greek loanword οὔτε 'neither, nor'
first part of ⲉⲡϩⲟⲥⲟⲛ split across line break; the conjunction continues into line 20
ⲟ restored medially; completes ⲉⲡϩⲟⲥⲟⲛ (Greek ἐφ' ὅσον) 'as long as'
ϥ̄ restored as 3sg.m object suffix; ⲛⲥⲉⲛⲧ- visible. Conjunctive 'and they bring him' (before the judge)
internal ⲧⲃ and ⲛⲉ restored, surrounding ⲙⲛ̄- and -ⲟⲟ- visible; the term ⲙⲛⲧⲃⲟⲟⲛⲉ recurs throughout this chapter
ϥ restored as 3sg.m subject of habitual; ϣⲁ visible. Combines with ⲕⲁ on line 27 → ϣⲁϥⲕⲁ 'he habitually places'
ⲁ visible, ⲛ restored. The particle ⲁⲛ 'also/again' confirming the parallel construction
single letter ⲗ of ⲧⲱⲃⲗⲱ 'recompense' split across line break — ⲧⲱⲃ̄- on line 28, -ⲱ on line 29
editor's restoration of relative + habitual prefix; introduces the souls' habitual action of listening to the Devil. Continues syntax to line 31
final ⲩ of ⲡⲡⲉⲑⲁⲩ 'the evil'; word completion only

first part of ⲉⲙⲁⲩⲡⲉⲓⲫⲉ split across line break; ⲡⲉⲓⲑⲉ (Greek πείθεσθαι) 'be persuaded, believe' negated. The phrase 'which they do not believe (will reach) unto...' fits the page-end and continues to next page

notes.decision: Translated 'our God' (= ⲡⲉⲛ-ⲛⲟⲩⲧⲉ with Lyc. ⲡⲁⲛ- contraction). The phrasing places the Apostle's prior assertion ('A Judge is our God') as the prompt for the Nazorean's challenge that follows.
Greek loanword ναζωραῖος 'Nazorean' — Manichaean polemical designation for a Jewish-Christian opponent. The split ⲡⲓⲛⲁⲍⲟ-/-ⲣⲉⲩⲥ across lines 1-2 is the manuscript's line-break.
Greek τορεία or ταυρέα 'whip (of bull-hide)' — translated 'whip' as the standard punitive instrument cited in this catalogue (whip / collar / sword).
Greek ἑρμητάριον — a punishment instrument, possibly a rod or staff used by court officers. Translated 'punishment-rod' interpretively; the verb ⲧⲙⲱⲣⲉ (Gk. τιμωρέω 'punish') governs it.
Latin/Greek κολλάριον 'iron collar, pillory.' Translated 'collar' — the third punitive instrument in the judge's catalogue.
ⲡ̄ here likely an abbreviation/scribal contraction for ⲣ̄ 'do' — yielding ϣⲁⲣⲉ ⲡⲕⲣⲓⲧⲏⲥ ⲣ̄ ⲛⲉⲓ̈ ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ 'the judge does all these.' Preserved the manuscript reading ⲡ̄ in coptic field.

ⲥⲁⲛ- prefix from ⲥⲁ- 'side, kinsman of, associate of' + ⲙⲛⲧⲃⲟⲟⲛⲉ 'wickedness' yields 'associate-of-wickedness' / 'one-on-the-side-of-wickedness.' Translated 'associate-of-wickedness' to preserve the categorial-belonging force absent from a flat 'wicked one.'

ⲃⲱⲗ 'release/dissolve' — per glossary, the dissolving complement to ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise.' Here applied to wickedness: the judge's work is to dissolve/undo wickedness rather than to multiply it. The semantic preserves the spatial-functional sense of unbinding.

ⲃⲱⲩ uncertain — possibly Lyc. dialectal/scribal form of ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'release/cast out' or related to ⲃⲱⲱⲩ 'be cast out, abandoned' (Crum 49a). Translated 'casting away the evil' to preserve the expulsive sense parallel to the surrounding ⲃⲱⲗ 'release' and ⲥⲱϩⲧ̄ 'sever.'
ⲛⲟⲩⲉ as a verb 'beat, strike' — opening the four-verb punitive series (beat / punish / slay / kill) that the Nazorean's challenge had ascribed to the judge.

ⲟⲩⲱⲥϥ 'shatter, smash, cut down' (cf. Sah. ⲟⲩⲱϣϥ̄). Combined with the following ⲥⲱϩⲧ̄ 'sever' the doublet expresses the surgical excision of evil from the man — the judge's act IS the cutting-away, not the wickedness itself.
Greek ἀμέλει γοῦν 'indeed at any rate, by all means' — discourse intensifier introducing the Apostle's clinching empirical observation about free good men beside the judge's tribunal.
Imperative ϯ ⲡⲉⲕϩⲏⲧ 'give your heart' = 'attend, pay attention.' Standard Coptic idiom for soliciting attention to a teaching.

Idiomatic phrase, uncertain. ⲧⲁⲡ = 'horn, head, top' (Crum 423b) likely used here in legal-punitive sense for 'reckoning' or 'person-as-account.' Translated 'draw their account' to preserve the judicial register: the judge does not summon them or draw on them legally as long as they are blameless.

Parsing: ⲙⲁϥ- (negative habitual 3sg) + ⲣ̄- + ϩⲁⲛ-ϩⲣ̄ⲧⲉ (indef. plural 'fears') + ⲁⲣⲁⲩ ('toward them'). Reading the 3sg as referring back to the men: 'they have no fears toward him' (alternatively 3sg.m 'he produces no fears in them'). The grammatical balance with surrounding clauses about the men favors the men-as-subject reading.

ⲃⲁⲡϥ uncertain — possibly Lyc. for ⲃⲱⲡ/ⲡⲱⲣⲡ̄ 'snatch' or a binding/hand-over verb. Translated 'and they bind him' provisionally; the action-sequence (seize / X / bring before judge) supports a securing-verb between apprehension and arraignment.

Habitual 3sg.m + ⲛ̄ (Lyc. for ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'bring') = 'he habitually brings.' The subject is the wrongdoer who has placed his own wickedness upon his own head — the chapter's central theodicy: the sinner is the source of his own punishment.
ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fill' + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth' as discourse-imperative: 'be filled out, be fully convinced.' Translated 'be filled out then and see' to preserve the spatial-cognitive metaphor of full inward conviction.
ⲯⲩⲭⲁⲩⲉ — Lycopolitan plural of Greek ψυχή 'soul' with -ⲁⲩⲉ pluralizer. Translated 'the souls' per terminology guide.

Greek πείθεσθαι 'be persuaded' (cf. accumulated vocabulary entry ⲡⲉⲓⲑⲉ). Restored ⲉⲙⲁⲩⲡⲉⲓ-ⲫⲉ 'they are not persuaded' = 'they do not believe' — the souls do this evil because they do not believe the consequences will reach them.
